concepts.title: India and Pakistan: Economic Development Path

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India and Pakistan: Economic Development Path' refers to.
questions.a: India and Pakistan, both part of British India until 1947, followed different development paths with India emphasising public-sector-led planning and Pakistan relying more on private enterprise and foreign aid.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Pakistan: Economic Development Path'.
questions.a: Despite a shared colonial past, India and Pakistan adopted contrasting economic strategies, leading to different growth and structural outcomes.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'India and Pakistan: Economic Development Path'.
questions.a: compare the development paths of India and Pakistan

concepts.title: India and China: Economic Development Path

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India and China: Economic Development Path' refers to.
questions.a: India and China, both large Asian economies, adopted different reform paths: China introduced market reforms in 1978 under communist rule, while India launched liberalisation in 1991 within a democratic framework.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and China: Economic Development Path'.
questions.a: China's reforms began earlier and emphasised export-led manufacturing, while India's reforms focused on services and a slower shift from planning to markets.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'India and China: Economic Development Path'.
questions.a: compare the development paths of India and China

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Demographic Indicators: India, Pakistan, China' refers to.
questions.a: Demographic indicators such as population size, growth rate, sex ratio, and fertility rate describe the population structure and dynamics of a country.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Demographic Indicators: India, Pakistan, China'.
questions.a: China's one-child policy slowed its population growth sharply, while India and Pakistan continue to have higher fertility and younger populations.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Demographic Indicators: India, Pakistan, China', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: annual_population_growth_rate = ((population_t1 - population_t0) / population_t0) * 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Development Indicators: A Comparison' refers to.
questions.a: Human development indicators such as life expectancy, literacy rate, infant mortality rate, and HDI rank measure the well-being of people beyond income.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Development Indicators: A Comparison'.
questions.a: China ranks highest on most human development indicators among the three, with India in the middle and Pakistan lagging on literacy and health.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Human Development Indicators: A Comparison'.
questions.a: compare the human development indicators of India, Pakistan, and China

concepts.title: Similarities and Differences Among India, Pakistan, China

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Similarities and Differences Among India, Pakistan, China' refers to.
questions.a: All three countries share a history of colonial or semi-colonial rule and planning, but differ in political system, reform timing, and sectoral focus of development.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Similarities and Differences Among India, Pakistan, China'.
questions.a: Despite shared starting points, differences in governance, reform strategy, and human capital investment produced divergent development outcomes.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Similarities and Differences Among India, Pakistan, China'.
questions.a: what are the similarities in the development of India, Pakistan, and China

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Lessons from India's Neighbours' refers to.
questions.a: Lessons from neighbours are policy insights India can draw from the development experiences of China and Pakistan, including the role of reforms, infrastructure, and human capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lessons from India's Neighbours'.
questions.a: India can learn from China's emphasis on infrastructure, manufacturing, and human capital, and avoid the pitfalls of political instability seen in Pakistan.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Lessons from India's Neighbours'.
questions.a: what lessons can India learn from China's development experience
